title: The webinar funnel drowning in cheap leads but starving on revenue
content: An edtech selling an INR 18,000 data-analytics course ran a YouTube + Meta funnel into a free Saturday webinar. On INR 38L/month it pulled ~9,500 registrations at an INR 400 CPL - the team felt great. But only 22% showed up and just 1.8% of registrants bought (171 buyers), so blended CAC hit INR 22,200 on an INR 18,000 ticket: ROAS 0.81, losing money on every sale. The team blamed the pitch and kept rewriting the closing offer. We pulled cohort data by source instead. Show-up was 41% for Google-search leads but 14% for Meta 'free webinar' interest sets - those leads came for a freebie, never to buy. The bottleneck was lead intent and the registration-to-webinar gap, not the pitch. Actions: cut broad Meta interest sets, added an INR 49 refundable registration fee, replaced email reminders with a 4-touch WhatsApp sequence (T-24h, T-3h, T-15min, replay), and moved the webinar to Wednesday 8 PM. Registrations fell to 5,200 at INR 520 CPL, but show-up rose to 38%, buy-rate to 4.1% (210 buyers), and CAC dropped to INR 12,800 - ROAS 1.4, revenue per rupee up 1.7x.
lesson: A cheap lead is not a cheap customer. When show-up and conversion break, audit intent by source before touching the pitch - if Meta 'free webinar' leads show up at a third of Google-search rates, you have an intent problem, not a copy problem. An INR 49 refundable fee plus WhatsApp-timed reminders filters tyre-kickers and lifts every downstream metric at once.
